bear_case: Three of five macro regime gates remain problematic heading into June 22: DXY at 100.75 (worsening on Juneteenth, not improving), VIX at 17.0 (at gate but not through it), and 30Y at 4.93% (7 bps from the 5.00% trigger). Warsh's 'no forward guidance' posture means any FOMC-adjacent communication event (June 22–26 Fed speaker calendar) can re-accelerate hawkish repricing without a clear dovish signal to anchor expectations. The BTC stop execution (Day 2 active at $62,520) is a risk-sentiment barometer: if the largest liquid risk asset can't hold $63,500 on Day 2 while Juneteenth ETF desks are dark and the Iran ceasefire is fully in effect, the Fed hawkish regime is more durable than the equity recovery from June 18 implied. If SPX opens June 22 below 7,460 (the regime floor), the BUY formally reverts to STEP_ASIDE and position sizing must be reduced across the portfolio. The 30Y approaching 5.00% is the most dangerous near-term trigger — a sustained breach simultaneously voids NVDA's conditional-add framework, compresses SPCX's multiple further, and generates institutional equity-to-bond reallocation headwinds.
